messages:
maria-peopleops: Heads up — we have a case from payroll migration: employee EMPLID 74521 had their 401(k) deferral changed from pre-tax to Roth for the last 4 pay periods AND company HSA contribution for Feb was not applied. Need guidance on corrective steps and tax implications.

allen-payroll: ugh — thanks for flagging. can you confirm whether the deductions physically posted to Roth buckets or were just remapped in the provider UI (i.e., cash flow still went to pre-tax)?

maria-peopleops: provider ledger shows contributions in Roth account. payroll register shows pre-tax deduction code, but vendor mapping sent it to Roth. HSA employer match shows $0 for Feb in vendor ledger but payroll had a liability created.

tom-payrollvendor: we pushed a mapping change during migration that affected code 401A -> routed to Roth instead of Pretax for that client mapping. apologies. we can reverse-map previous 4 weeks entries and do journal reversals on provider side — but we need payroll to issue corrected payroll files for tax reporting.

natalie-finance: if the provider posts reversals, we still need payroll to produce corrected YTD wages for W-2. For employee side: moving pre-tax -> Roth means taxes were underwithheld originally? Actually Roth contributions are post-tax, so employee likely underpaid FICA/Medicare? we should consult tax.

sarah-hrbp: employee is asking if they have to pay penalties. also they turned 50 in March and started catch-up contributions that month. how does that affect totals if we retro-change earlier entries?

allen-payroll: ok checklist proposal: 1) vendor to reverse the 4 Roth credits and re-post as Pretax 401k; 2) payroll to run off-cycle corrective payroll adjusting taxable wages if necessary; 3) HR to notify employee and get consent for corrections where needed; 4) benefits to reapply Feb HSA employer contribution and confirm deposit.

benefits-bot: FYI: Plan document requires participant-level consent for corrective distributions >60 days in some cases. Please confirm plan year rules before executing reversals.

maria-peopleops: noted. Tom can you confirm vendor can produce a reversal file we can feed back into payroll by EOD tomorrow? If vendor needs signed authorization, what form?

tom-payrollvendor: we can produce reversal + reallocation file. we need a signed vendor correction authorization (I can attach a template). Also need payroll to provide net pay detail and tax indicators.

allen-payroll: payroll can run an off-cycle correction. Quick Q: do we treat the Roth->Pretax swap as an employer-caused error and therefore make it a pretax reclassification with no employee tax outlay? we should loop in outside tax counsel, but for payroll operations we can prepare a corrective draw that adjusts federal/state withholding and employer taxes.

natalie-finance: looped tax counsel (copied) — but a pragmatic route is: reverse Roth postings on vendor, re-post as pretax, then issue corrective W-2 (W-2c) if needed. For HSA: reissue Feb employer deposit; if missed and plan document proration applies, we should calculate retro employer match pro rata and put into employee HSA account ASAP.

sarah-hrbp: I'll draft the employee notification language: short note, explain what happened, expected timeline for correction, whether they'll see a net-pay adjustment, and payroll contact. will share for review.

maria-peopleops: thanks. action items: Tom attach correction authorization + timeline, Allen prepare off-cycle payroll worksheet and tax impact estimate, Natalie confirm whether HSA deposit should be gross-up for missed employer pre-tax funding? Sarah draft employee note. target: corrections posted by next Friday.

tom-payrollvendor: attaching template in thread (will send via email too). we can meet Wed to walk through files.

allen-payroll: we may need to withhold the employee's consent for any net-pay reclaims. if we adjust taxable wages retro, employees should be notified and given an opt-out window per policy. i'll include that in the note.

maria-peopleops: okay all — thanks. tagging next steps in linear ticket and will close when W-2s/HSA show corrected. @sarah-hrbp ping me if employee escalates. :thumbsup:
